'''{{transliteration|ar|Hergma}}'''{{efn|also ''hregma'',<ref name="L'Harmattan"/> ''ḥarqma''<ref name=Wright/>}} ({{langx|ar|الهركمة}}, {{literal translation|trotter}} ([[synecdoche]]);<ref name=Fox/> {{langx|ary|كرعين|translit='''kerʻine'''}};<ref name=Assimil/>{{efn|also ''kour3ine''<ref name="Benlafquih"/>}} {{langx|arq|لوبيا بالكرعين|'''loubia bil kerʻine'''}};<ref name=Mourad/> {{langx|zgh|ⵉⴼⵏⵣⴰ}}, {{transliteration|zgh|ifenza}}<ref name=Laoust/>) is a [[Maghrebi cuisine]] stew featuring stewed [[trotters]]. The dish is largely cooked on [[Eid al-Adha]] with the trotters of the [[Qurban (Islamic ritual sacrifice)|sacrificial animal]], but also served year-round at ''[[souk]]s,'' and enjoyed during [[Ramadan]].<ref name=Wright/> In [[Moroccan cuisine]], ''hergma'' is a [[tagine]]; in [[Tunisian cuisine]], ''hergma'' is a [[lablabi]] featuring other [[offal]] along with the trotters, such as [[heart as food|heart]] and [[tripe]].
